newsitem.title: USA: Maine starts federal tax credit program for jobs.
newsitem.headline: Maine starts federal tax credit program for jobs.

text.p: Maine said Wednesday it began to enroll employers in a federal program that gives them tax credits for hiring disadvantaged workers, though the program's details still are being negotiated with Washington.
The one-year program was scheduled to begin today but the federal government did not give at least some states much advance assistance.
"We had two weeks to pull this together so everything is catch-as-catch can," said Kathleen Piecuch, supervisor, special projects, with the state Department of Labor.

The federal program, which revamps a similar effort that ended in 1994, gives tax credits to companies that hire people who are collecting welfare benefits, like Aid for Families with Dependent Children and Food Stamps.

Veterans who qualify for those programs also are eligible, as are people who were convicted of a felony within the past year, provided they meet income guidelines, and people with disabilities who participate in certain government programs.

The state official could not immediately estimate how many workers in Maine might be eligible. Companies can get credits for up to 35 percent of $6,000 in qualified first-year wages, for a maximum of $2,100, she explained.
